Natural gas prices in Europe started the week with a rise to 96.075 euros per MWh, gaining 8.6% from Friday as weather forecasts saw colder weather coming to the continent, which is struggling with record-low inventories.

The benchmark TTF price is equal to $105.49 per MWh and is the highest daily price rise in over a week, Bloomberg reported today.

Even though the TTF price has dropped from the four-year high of over 100 euros per MWh reached in late October, Europe’s benchmark gas price has now nearly tripled from $33 (30 euros) per MWh at this time last year.

War-related LNG export disruption from the Middle East is the biggest reason for the price rise, as QatarEnergy’s force majeure sent LNG spot market prices significantly higher, sapping demand from European gas traders during the summer, which is normally the most active storage refill season. Traders apparently held off on major buying in anticipation of a reversal in the price trend, and when it did not come, European countries entered winter with much lower than normal inventory levels.

Europe has not only entered the heating season with the lowest gas levels in storage sites in over a decade, but it is also estimated to have withdrawn in recent weeks 10% of the gas injected during the summer filling season, leaving supply vulnerable to potentially extreme cold winter weather.

As of Sunday, the European Union’s gas storage facilities were 69.17% full, holding approximately 781 TWh of gas, with injections totaling 714.16 GWh and withdrawals reaching 2,868.4 GWh, according to official data from Gas Infrastructure Europe.

The supply situation is about to tighten further, as the ban on Russian gas imports enters into effect in January. European importers have been gobbling up almost all the LNG produced at Novatek’s Yamal LNG facility this year, generating 8.7 billion euros, or $9.57 billion in proceeds for the Russian gas major.
